To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

trade, aid, and foreign direct investments (FDI) are significant in determining migration flows in the short run, but only trade is significant in the long run, whereas remittances are significant in both the short and long run.
trade, aid, FDI and remittances are important factors in managing migration from Turkey to Germany in the short as in the long-run.
trade, aid, remittances and FDI are all relevant for migration from Turkey to Germany.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two main questions: (i) what determines the volume of international migration?
the role of trade and factor movements as a substitute for migration.
the question of whether trade and factor flows can be used as policy instruments to curb migration from Turkey to Germany.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of trade, aid, FDI and remittances on migration are mixed and that migration is mainly driven by the income differential between the two countries.
trade and factor flow effects on migration are ambiguous and depend on the specific situation.
the effects of trade, aid, remittances and foreign direct investment on migration are not unambiguous.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trade and factor movements can curb the migration from Turkey to Germany.
the Turkish government should not rely solely on the income effect in order to curb the outflow of Turkish migrants to Germany.
the effects of the dynamic gains from international trade and factor flows in reducing migration from Turkey are not clear and the effects are mixed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
migration is not a zero-sum game.
migration can be managed better if the gains from trade, aid, and factor flows are taken into account.
trade and factor movements are important in managing migration in the long run, but the income differential is the most important determinant of migration.
